title: Batch and parallel optimization orchestration
description:
Purpose: Run complete multi-target feedback analysis and optimization workflows efficiently with bounded concurrency, stable ordering, isolated mutations, and explicit coverage.

Exclusions:
- Silent sampling of complete-scope requests.
- Shared mutable candidate state across targets.
- Unbounded concurrency or automatic production promotion.

Dependencies: Consumes discovery output, supported runtime interfaces, reproducible cohorts, and the shared run-evidence contract. Existing batch-read and batch-dispatch capabilities remain the foundation.

Definition of Done:
- Complete-scope workflows enumerate and report every target or explicitly report incomplete coverage.
- Batch input and result ordering and opaque identifiers remain unchanged.
- Concurrency and resource use are bounded and configurable.
- Target failures remain isolated and visible without discarding successful results.
- Planning artifacts are portable between supported local and hosted execution.
- Existing single-target APIs remain compatible.
- Behavior-first specifications and focused tests pass.

Running log: Preserve existing issue histories and record sanitized decisions, attempts, outcomes, and next steps in this epic or its child issues.

comments.author: derek
comments.text:
As an AI agent developer, I want efficient batch operations for feedback alignment and optimizer dispatch via execute_tactus, so that scorecard-wide analysis and optimization workflows scale to dozens of scores without excessive API latency.

Success criteria:
- Scorecard-wide feedback alignment completes in 1-2 API calls instead of N calls (one per score)
- Batch optimizer dispatch API exists for multi-score optimization scenarios
- Documentation accurately reflects the Tactus API surface
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing single-score APIs
